subject: maths
pattern: Determinants carries 10-12 marks in the Karnataka 2nd PUC maths paper, one of the heavier chapters: 1-mark questions on minor, cofactor, singular matrix and |adj A|, 2-3 mark questions on area of a triangle, properties of determinants and inverse by adjoint, and a compulsory 5-mark question on solving a system of three linear equations by the matrix method. Examiners expect |A|, the cofactors, adj A and A inverse to be shown step by step, followed by the solution and a check.

questions.q: When is a square matrix said to be singular? Write the condition for $A^{-1}$ to exist.
questions.answer: A square matrix $A$ is singular if $|A|=0$. $A^{-1}$ exists only if $A$ is non-singular, i.e. $|A|\neq0$.

questions.q: If $A$ is a square matrix of order 3 with $|A|=4$, find $|\operatorname{adj}A|$.
questions.answer: For a square matrix of order $n$, $|\operatorname{adj}A|=|A|^{n-1}$. So $|\operatorname{adj}A|=4^{2}=16$.

questions.q: Write the minor of the element $a_{23}$ in the determinant $\begin{vmatrix}1&2&3\\4&5&6\\7&8&9\end{vmatrix}$.
Find the values of $k$ if the area of the triangle with vertices $(k,0)$, $(4,0)$, $(0,2)$ is 4 square units.
questions.answer: Area $=\tfrac12\begin{vmatrix}k&0&1\\4&0&1\\0&2&1\end{vmatrix}=\tfrac12\,|k(0-2)-0+1(8-0)|=\tfrac12|-2k+8|$. Given area $=4$: $|-2k+8|=8$. So $-2k+8=8$ gives $k=0$, or $-2k+8=-8$ gives $k=8$. Hence $k=0$ or $k=8$.

questions.q: Using properties of determinants, show that $\begin{vmatrix}1&a&b+c\\1&b&c+a\\1&c&a+b\end{vmatrix}=0$.
questions.answer: Apply $C_3\to C_3+C_2$. The third column becomes $(a+b+c,\ a+b+c,\ a+b+c)$. Taking $(a+b+c)$ common from $C_3$, we get $(a+b+c)\begin{vmatrix}1&a&1\\1&b&1\\1&c&1\end{vmatrix}$. Columns $C_1$ and $C_3$ are identical, so the determinant is $0$.

questions.q: Using determinants, find the equation of the line joining $(1,2)$ and $(3,6)$.
questions.answer: For any point $(x,y)$ on the line the three points are collinear, so $\begin{vmatrix}x&y&1\\1&2&1\\3&6&1\end{vmatrix}=0$. Expanding along $R_1$: $x(2-6)-y(1-3)+1(6-6)=0$, i.e. $-4x+2y=0$. Hence the line is $y=2x$.

questions.q: Find the adjoint of the matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{bmatrix}$.
questions.answer: For a $2\times2$ matrix $\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix}$, $\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{bmatrix}$ (interchange the diagonal elements, change the signs of the others). Hence $\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}4&-2\\-3&1\end{bmatrix}$.

questions.q: Using properties of determinants, prove that $\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\a&b&c\\a^2&b^2&c^2\end{vmatrix}=(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)$.
questions.answer: Apply $C_1\to C_1-C_2$ and $C_2\to C_2-C_3$. $C_1=(0,\ a-b,\ a^2-b^2)$, $C_2=(0,\ b-c,\ b^2-c^2)$. Take $(a-b)$ common from $C_1$ and $(b-c)$ from $C_2$: $(a-b)(b-c)\begin{vmatrix}0&0&1\\1&1&c\\a+b&b+c&c^2\end{vmatrix}$. Expand along $R_1$: $(a-b)(b-c)\,[(b+c)-(a+b)]=(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)$.

questions.q: Find $A^{-1}$ for $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&-3&5\\3&2&-4\\1&1&-2\end{bmatrix}$ and use it to solve $2x-3y+5z=11$, $3x+2y-4z=-5$, $x+y-2z=-3$.
